value: basking activity peak between 11:00 and 12:30 h (daytime observations 8:00-18:30 h)
method: visual counts of sun-basking turtles with binoculars from fixed observation points at the pond edges, each pond visited once in each of three parts of the day (morning 8:00-11:30, midday 11:30-15:00, afternoon 15:00-18:30), 5 survey days per season per year
conditions: Free-living turtles in a dammed valley pond system (Babat valley, Gödöllő, Hungary), 2015 and 2016; spring mid-April to mid-May, summer July, autumn September; only basking turtles were counted, so the value is the timing of basking at the surface, and observations covered 8:00-18:30 h only (no night observation). The cited sentence pools both years and all seasons; the paper also reports that the peak was between 11:00 and 12:30 h in spring and summer but between 12:30 and 14:00 h in autumn (Results; Abstract). Basking numbers correlated positively with temperatures and the seasonal maximum of basking was in spring. Sex, age and size were not recorded and no marking is described. No bait or lure is described.
where: Results, Finer time scale basking activity pattern
quote: The cumulative number of observed basking turtles per 1.5-hours interval (both years and all seasons), i.e. the peak of basking activity, was highest between 11:00 and 12:30 h.
